title: Do Rolling Chairs and Heavy Furniture Dent Vinyl Plank?
meta: Rolling chairs rarely dent quality vinyl plank; small hard feet under heavy furniture do. Wills Flooring explains cores, wear layers and fixes for Sammamish.
keywords: do rolling chairs damage vinyl plank, heavy furniture dent vinyl plank flooring, LVP indentation piano, office chair on luxury vinyl plank, vinyl plank flooring Sammamish WA, SPC vs WPC dents

blocks.lead: A rigid-core vinyl plank with a 20 mil wear layer handles rolling office chairs fine; what dents vinyl plank is a heavy object on a tiny hard foot, like a piano leg or a bed frame on quarter-size glides.
blocks.detail: Vinyl is a plastic, so it deforms under a concentrated load and mostly recovers when the load moves. Whether the mark stays depends on the core, the wear layer, how flat the subfloor is and how wide the foot is. All four are things you control.

blocks.html: This question comes up on almost every Sammamish estimate, because the houses here are big and so is what goes in them. A Trossachs main floor has a home office with two rolling chairs, a Klahanie family room has a ten-foot sectional and a 75 inch TV console, and a Pine Lake dining room has a piano that came from grandma. People love vinyl plank for the dogs and the mud, then worry it will look like a golf green after a year. Here is what actually dents it, what does not, and how to set up each room.

items.title: Pounds per square inch, not pounds
items.text: A 400 lb fridge on four 1 in feet is 100 psi at each foot. The same fridge on a 2 by 3 ft rolling tray is almost nothing. Vinyl does not care how heavy the object is. It cares how small the contact point is.

items.title: A soft or thin core
items.text: Flexible glue-down planks and softer WPC (wood-plastic) cores give more under a point load. SPC (stone-plastic) cores are dense and compress far less, which is why they are the default in busy homes.

items.title: Hollow spots under the plank
items.text: A floating plank bridging a low spot in the subfloor has nothing under it. Step on it with a chair leg and it flexes down and can crack the locking edge. Most "dents" in a new floor are really subfloor dips.

items.title: Heat plus weight
items.text: Vinyl softens as it warms. A heavy planter in a south-facing window or a couch leg over a heat register sits on a softer plank all summer and leaves a mark it would not leave in a cool room.

blocks.note: Rolling itself does not dent a rigid plank. Wear-layer thickness decides whether years of rolling dull the finish; 20 mil holds up in a home office, 12 mil is a bedroom rating.

items.text: Never roll them across bare plank; the small rear wheels gouge. Lay a sheet of hardboard down first. Once in place, the appliance feet are wide enough not to dent a rigid core.

The highest-risk item in the house: 500 to 1,000 lb on three or four brass wheels. Use piano caster cups, the wide ones, and expect slight marks under them over years regardless of flooring. Every hard floor gets these.
Metal bed frames with quarter-size feet are worse than the piano because they get bounced on nightly. Screw on 2 in felt glides or set the frame on wide furniture cups.
Weight is spread across many legs; risk is low. The issue is dragging them for cleaning, which scratches. Felt pads on every leg, replaced yearly.
Do not install a floating plank floor under a fixed island. Pinning the floor stops it from moving and it buckles at the nearest doorway. Islands go down first; plank floats around them with a gap.

blocks.title: The subfloor is the real dent protection:
blocks.text: Most Sammamish plateau homes from the 1990s and 2000s have OSB subfloors with seams that have cupped a little over the years. A plank over a raised seam has a hollow on either side. That is where the chair leg goes through the locking edge. We flatten before we install, and you should insist any installer does the same.
When vinyl plank is the wrong choice for the room

items.html: A home gym with a power rack or dropped barbells. No residential plank is rated for that. Use rubber gym tile over the plank or instead of it.
A sunroom that hits 100 degrees. Heat softens vinyl and expands it. Combine that with heavy furniture and you get permanent impressions and peaked seams. Check our sunroom post before you commit.
You want a floor that shows zero marks under a piano. Nothing does that, not hardwood, not tile grout lines, not vinyl. Caster cups and acceptance are the answer.
The subfloor is badly out of flat and you will not fix it. Plank over a wavy floor will crack at the edges no matter how good the core. Fix the floor or choose carpet.

blocks.text: Set up the room so it never dents

items.html: Buy a 20 mil SPC plank for the main floor. The wear layer handles the casters; the core handles the loads. Ask what the plank's static-load rating is; good ones publish it.
Get the subfloor flattened before install. We check flatness at the free estimate and price any patching separately, so you know before day one.
Swap every office chair to soft casters. Do it the day the floor goes in, before anyone forgets.
Put wide glides under anything over 200 lb. Felt for things you drag, hard wide cups for things that stay put. Recheck the felt every fall when the dog hair gets bad.

Keep the spare carton. If a plank ever does crack, a click-lock floor can have that plank replaced. Wills Flooring's vinyl plank installation carries a 1-year workmanship warranty, and the manufacturer covers the wear layer.

faq.q: Will an office chair ruin vinyl plank flooring?
faq.a: Not a rigid-core plank with a 20 mil wear layer and soft polyurethane casters. Hard nylon wheels grind grit into the finish over years and dull it. Swap the wheels, keep them clean, and skip soft clear PVC mats, which can stain vinyl.

faq.q: Can I put a piano on luxury vinyl plank?
faq.a: Yes, on wide piano caster cups. A piano puts several hundred pounds on three or four small wheels, which will mark any floor over time, including hardwood. The cups spread the load and the marks stay minor and hidden.

faq.q: Do dents in vinyl plank come back out?
faq.a: Light impressions from furniture often recover over days once the load is moved, faster with gentle warmth from a hair dryer. A crushed core or a cracked locking edge does not recover; that plank gets replaced, which is easy on a click-lock floor.

faq.q: Is SPC or WPC better for heavy furniture?
faq.a: SPC. Its stone-polymer core is denser and compresses less under narrow feet. WPC is softer and quieter and works well in bedrooms, but for a Sammamish main floor with a piano, an office and a sectional we install SPC.

faq.q: How much does it cost to install vinyl plank in a Sammamish home office and family room?
faq.a: Wills Flooring charges $2.50 per sq ft for installation labor with a 500 sq ft minimum. A 320 sq ft office plus 480 sq ft family room is 800 × $2.50 = $2,000 in labor; the plank, underlayment and any subfloor flattening are quoted at the free estimate.

faq.q: Should I put a chair mat on vinyl plank?
faq.a: You do not need one with soft casters and a good wear layer. If you want one, choose polycarbonate or a felt-backed mat. Soft clear PVC mats can react with the vinyl and leave a yellowed rectangle that never comes out.
